punchline: The best-known study of the Wim Hof breathing method compared just 12 trained volunteers with 12 untrained ones.
thirty_sec: Wim Hof's basic breathing is 30 to 40 deep breaths, a hold after the last exhale, then one deep breath held for 10 to 15 seconds, repeated three or four times. At Radboud University, 12 trained volunteers and 12 untrained ones received endotoxin, and the trained group reported fewer flu-like symptoms. It was a small trial, and doing the breathing near water can be deadly.
